core_obligations: The object formula (proof lines 2466-2470): (cosk_m U)_n is defined as the limit of U over (Delta/[n])_{<=m}^{opp}, which exists since C has finite limits and the index category is finite.

Mapping property, morphisms into cosk (lines 2472-2483): a morphism gamma : V -> cosk_m U is a family of maps gamma(alpha) : V_n -> U_k over alpha : [k] -> [n], k <= m, compatible with the simplicial structures; the displayed commutativity constraints with n = k = k', varphi = alpha', alpha = psi = id force gamma(alpha') = gamma(id_[k]) circ V(alpha'), so gamma is determined by the gamma(id_[k]), k <= m, and these assemble into a morphism sk_m V -> U.

Mapping property, converse (lines 2485-2490): given gamma : sk_m V -> U, the family gamma(alpha) = gamma(id_[k]) circ V(alpha) satisfies all the displayed commutativity restraints and hence gives a morphism V -> cosk_m U; the two constructions are inverse, establishing the mapping property and hence existence of the functor cosk_m.
proof_roadmap: Define cosk_m U level-wise by the limit formula.
Unwind a morphism V -> cosk_m U into compatible families and show it is determined by sk_m V -> U.
Rebuild the morphism from a map sk_m V -> U and conclude the adjunction.
difficulty_reason: Existence lemma (statement 2450-2464, proof 2466-2506): the coskeleton is constructed by the limit formula and its universal property is proven in both directions through an explicit unfolding of the limit and the displayed commutativity constraints; the assembly of the gamma(id_[k]) into a truncated morphism is the objectwise restatement of the definition (source line 2483). H2: formal category-theoretic construction.
